legend: More than 50% of the acini in a terminal duct lobular unit are filled and expanded by loosely cohesive monomorphic cells with scant cytoplasm and small uniform nuclei.

Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ is characterized by a solid proliferation of dyscohesive cells, similar to classic lobular carcinoma in situ, but with marked nuclear pleomorphism equivalent to high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ.
Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ lacks membranous E-cadherin expression.

diagnosis: Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ with apocrine differentiation
legend: A subset of pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ is further characterized by apocrine features, based on large cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and round to oval nuclei containing prominent nucleoli.

diagnosis: Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ with apocrine differentiation
legend: Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ is often associated with comedonecrosis and calcifications, leading to mammographic detection.

Florid lobular carcinoma in situ has cytological features similar to those of classic lobular carcinoma in situ (type A and/or type B cells) but is distinguished by marked expansion of terminal duct lobular units with little to no intervening stroma between markedly distended acini of involved terminal duct lobular units.
In florid lobular carcinoma in situ, the acini or ducts are markedly expanded (filling at least one HPF, equivalent to > 40–50 cells in diameter) and often associated with central necrosis.

In classic lobular carcinoma in situ, a mixture of small cells with uniform hyperchromatic nuclei (1–1.5 times the size of a lymphocyte, type A cells) and cells with slightly larger vesicular nuclei, small nucleoli, and larger cytoplasm (2 times the size of a lymphocyte, type B cells) is frequently observed.

diagnosis: Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ with apocrine differentiation
legend: Apocrine features may be observed in pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ with typically large cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and highly atypical nuclei containing prominent nucleoli.

diagnosis: Florid lobular carcinoma in situ with comedonecrosis
legend: The presence of comedonecrosis is common in florid and pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ, where it is often fragmented with loose apoptotic cells intermingled with vital cells forming an irregularly shaped luminal margin.

diagnosis: E-cadherin staining in pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ with apocrine features
legend: Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ with apocrine features lacks membranous expression of E-cadherin.

diagnosis: Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ with signet-ring morphology
legend: Signet-ring cells can occasionally be seen in association with pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ; however, the presence of signet-ring cells may be seen in association with any lobular carcinoma in situ subtype.
Marked distension of acinar structures with a very low amount of intervening stroma is appreciated in florid lobular carcinoma in situ.

legend: Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ is characterized by a solid proliferation of discohesive cells with marked nuclear pleomorphism. It is often associated with prominent enlargement of the involved ducts with comedonecrosis and calcifications.
Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ often shows the presence of multinucleated cells in association with cells with marked nuclear pleomorphism.
Terminal duct lobular unit showing moderate expansion of > 50% of the acini by dyscohesive monomorphic cells.

diagnosis: Mixed florid lobular carcinoma in situ and ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: Mixed ductal carcinoma in situ showing cribriform proliferation within the duct in the upper left and florid lobular carcinoma in situ showing acinar dilation in the lower right.

diagnosis: Mixed florid lobular carcinoma in situ and ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: E-cadherin is positive in the upper left ductal carcinoma in situ and negative in the lower right florid lobular carcinoma in situ.

legend: Low-power H&E stain shows a solid proliferation of dyscohesive monomorphic epithelial cells expanding > 50% of the acini in a terminal duct lobular unit.
Low-power H&E stain shows that the acini in a terminal duct lobular unit are involved with discohesive monomorphic epithelial cells.
Immunostaining shows that the neoplastic cells lack membranous E-cadherin expression. In contrast, the normal ducts maintain the membranous E-cadherin expression.

diagnosis: Florid lobular carcinoma in situ with apocrine differentiation
legend: Proliferation in enlarged acini of eosinophilic lobular carcinoma cells accompanied by central debris with little intervening stroma.

diagnosis: Florid lobular carcinoma in situ with apocrine differentiation
legend: E-cadherin–negative staining confirms a diagnosis of florid lobular carcinoma in situ.

High-power magnification of florid LCIS shows the cytological detail of mixed type A and type B cells. In the lower left corner is a zone of comedo-type necrosis with an irregular necrotic border at the interphase between vital cells and luminal space.

Florid LCIS is characterized by markedly distended acini or ducts with scant or no intervening stroma in between. The acini or ducts involved in florid LCIS span a diameter of ~40–50 cells. Comedo-type necrosis is frequently present in florid LCIS.
High-power magnification shows florid LCIS constituted mainly by type B cells.

The cells show incomplete and weak membranous E-cadherin staining in combination with complete loss of expression by immunohistochemistry. This pattern is also referred to as aberrant E-cadherin staining and is consistent with the diagnosis of LCIS.

Diffuse cytoplasmatic expression of p120 instead of strong membranous staining is observed in the same cell population. This staining pattern in combination with equivocal or aberrant E-cadherin expression further confirm the diagnosis of LCIS.

diagnosis: Florid lobular carcinoma in situ with microinvasion
legend: High-power magnification demonstrates markedly dilated ducts with florid lobular carcinoma in situ.

diagnosis: Florid lobular carcinoma in situ with microinvasion
legend: The antibody cocktail ADH5 (CK5/14, p63, and CK7/18) highlights the presence of a focus of microinvasion in the upper right corner in the absence of myoepithelial cells (cells in red expressing CK7/18 breaking out of the basement membrane) while the duct involved by florid lobular carcinoma in situ retains the outer myoepithelial layer (cells stained in brown with CK5/14 and p63 antibodies).

diagnosis: Atypical lobular hyperplasia and lobular carcinoma in situ
legend: Breast tissue with lobular neoplasia encompassing both atypical lobular hyperplasia and lobular carcinoma in situ (classic pattern). Radial scars, collagenous spherulosis and scattered calcifications are also seen.

diagnosis: Lobular carcinoma in situ with classic and pleomorphic apocrine features
legend: Core biopsy shows Lobular carcinoma in situ with both classic and pleomorphic apocrine features. The pleomorphic LCIS component shows necrosis and calcifications.

Pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ is characterized by a solid proliferation of dyshesive cells with marked nuclear pleomorphism. It is often associated with prominent enlargement of involved ducts with comedo necrosis and calcifications.

diagnosis: Pleomrphic Lobular Carcinoma in Situ with signet ring cells
legend: Signet ring cells characterized by typical intracytoplasmatic vacuoles can be appreciated in all LCIS subtypes including pLCIS.

diagnosis: Florid lobular carcinoma in situ in association with classic LCIS and ALH
legend: Marked distension of acinar structures with very low amount of intervening stroma is appreciated. In the periphery foci of classic LCIS are also present.

diagnosis: Florid LCIS in association with ALH and classic LCIS
legend: Markedly distended lobular units characterized by solid proliferation of dyshesive cells, are associated with zones with ALH and classic LCIS.
